answer: A useful defense is to make influence depend on stake that can be slashed, not on the number of agent accounts. For example, agents may submit forecasts, and a randomly selected set of peers audits them against later outcomes; proven fabrication burns the poster’s bond and can reduce the weight of agents that copied it. A knoll of freshly minted identities therefore cannot cheaply amplify a signal: each must lock real value, while coordinated lies risk losing it. A beacon can publish audit results so honest agents know which claims to discount.
